The World Table

An interactive culinary compendium — recipes, lexicon & study — every dish serves four unless noted

Recipes·Cuisines·Lexicon Terms

The Path of Study

A guided curriculum through the five hundred — ten semesters from first omelette to restaurateur’s capstone. Each course lists its dishes in teaching order and the Lexicon reading that explains why they work. Cook in sequence; the techniques compound.

The Screening Room

Twelve films worth studying frame by frame — a canon of technique on camera. Every recipe in the guide also carries its own Film school links: the dish itself, the techniques inside it, and a master to learn from.

Foundation · Eggs

Pépin’s Omelet Techniques

The most famous cooking lesson on film. Two omelets, one pan, sixty years of craft — watch his wrist, not the eggs.

 Foundation · Knife & Basics

Ramsay’s Five Basic Skills

Sharpening, the onion dice, rice, and more in one sitting. The claw grip alone repays the watch.

 Pastry · Lamination

Saffitz’s Croissants

A two-day project filmed honestly — every fold, chill, and proof. Lamination is temperature management; here is the proof.

 Fermentation

Maangchi’s Tongbaechu Kimchi

The definitive napa cabbage kimchi from the woman who taught the internet Korean food — salting, paste, and the onggi.

 Live Fire

BBQ with Franklin: The Brisket

Austin’s brisket king on trim, rub, fire, and patience. Salt, pepper, post oak — and hours you cannot rush.

 Dough · High Heat

Civitiello’s Neapolitan Pizza at Home

A world pizza champion adapts the true Neapolitan method to a home oven, via ItaliaSquisita — the slap, the stretch, the cornicione.

 Butchery

Pépin’s Chicken Galantine

A whole chicken deboned in minutes, then rebuilt as a galantine — the knife lesson every cook should watch twice.

 The Wok

How to Make Any Fried Rice

Chinese Cooking Demystified’s framework film — one technique, three flavors, and the logic to improvise any fried rice from what you have.

 Street Noodles

Pailin’s Best Pad Thai

The complete tutorial from Hot Thai Kitchen — tamarind balance, noodle timing, and the wok choreography of Thailand’s most famous dish.

 The Levant

Middle Eats’ Smoothest Hummus

An obsessive pursuit of silk — chickpea skins, tahini order, ice water — that settles the texture question for good.

 Bread & Wild Yeast

Weissman’s Sourdough Starter

The starter guide that launched a million jars — feeding ratios, timing, and what a ready levain actually looks like.

 The Braise

Panlasang Pinoy’s Killer Adobo

The Philippines’ national dish from its most trusted teacher — soy, vinegar, garlic, and the reduction that lacquers the chicken.
